subsystems.name: Optical neuron
subsystems.role: emits or modulates light in response to input, mimicking a neuron's firing.
parts: laser or modulator with nonlinear response

subsystems.name: Optical synapse
subsystems.role: weights connections between neurons by attenuating or phase-shifting light.

subsystems.name: Photonic interconnect
subsystems.role: routes and combines light signals across the chip.

subsystems.name: Photodetector array
subsystems.role: converts optical signals to electrical for readout and hybrid electronic control.

subsystems.name: Electronic control layer
subsystems.role: configures weights, supplies power, and handles I/O and calibration.

buildSteps.title: Design the network
buildSteps.detail: Map a neural network onto a photonic circuit: neurons, synapses, and interconnects, choosing wavelengths and layout.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the photonic chip
buildSteps.detail: Use silicon photonics or similar foundry processes to etch waveguides, modulators, and detectors on a wafer.

buildSteps.title: Integrate light sources
buildSteps.detail: Bond or grow lasers on-chip, or couple external lasers, to supply the light that carries signals.

buildSteps.title: Add weight-setting elements
buildSteps.detail: Deposit phase-change or other tunable materials on each synapse, then pattern them for individual control.

buildSteps.title: Co-package with electronics
buildSteps.detail: Flip-chip or monolithically integrate CMOS control circuits for driving, readout, and weight updates.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Measure each neuron and synapse, compensating for fabrication variations, and train the network using in-situ or external feedback.

buildSteps.title: Scale and validate
buildSteps.detail: Build larger arrays and test them on real tasks such as image recognition, comparing accuracy and power against electronic accelerators.

prerequisites.why: mature foundries can make low-loss waveguides and modulators at scale.
heterogeneous integration of III-V lasers on silicon is demonstrated but not yet standard in commercial photonic chips.
all-optical neurons are demonstrated but often need high power or special materials; many designs use electro-optic conversion instead.
phase-change materials can store weights optically, but endurance and stability are still being improved.
combining CMOS and photonics on one chip is possible but complex and costly.

pathway.milestone: small-scale photonic neural networks that perform simple classification tasks
pathway.unlocks: proof that optical neurons and synapses can learn.

pathway.milestone: electronic-photonic chips that accelerate matrix multiplication for AI inference
pathway.unlocks: lower power in data centres for specific workloads.

pathway.milestone: on-chip lasers, modulators, and non-volatile weights in a single process
mass-produced chips for always-on AI in cameras and sensors
